correctness.rationale: Equation (5.4) is specialized explicitly in RESULT.md. Sum/difference modal separation yields characteristic factors \(P_s(z)=(1+t)z^2-(1-K)z-K\), \(P_q(z)=(1+t)z^2-(1-c)z-c\) and one zero root, with \(K=2d^2-c>-1\). The three real-quadratic Schur inequalities are \(t>0\), \(2+t-2K>0\), \(1+t+K>0\) for the symmetric factor; q has \(K=c<1\). Thus strict stability iff \(hb>4d^2-2-2c\), equality has \(z=-1\), and smaller positive steps have \(z<-1\). Exact continuous modal masses are \(1+K\) and \(1+c\). Constant-history root expansions prove first-order convergence for \(K<1\); the parity formula at \(K=1\) proves the endpoint; \(K>1\) has nonzero \(O(h)\) excitation of a root tending to \(-K<-1\), hence fixed-time divergence. An actual SymPy characteristic-factorization assertion and numerical mode tests were executed from the attached verify.py and recorded as verify_output.txt. These computations are checks, not the proof.

value.rationale: The exact classification resolves a mathematically motivated gap emphasized by the source numerical sharpness study. It identifies a nontrivial signed cross-coupling cancellation: stability is governed by \(2d^2\leq1+c\) instead of the sufficient \(2d^2+c\leq1\), with an entire physically coercive stable range missed by the theorem (notably \(c\geq1/3\) under its additional scalar inf–sup hypothesis). Beyond the threshold, increasing the step size actually restores strict Schur stability, a structural anti-CFL effect. The boundary first-order convergence proof distinguishes numerical stability at positive steps from the limiting root -1. This is useful as an exact benchmark for tri-field lagging, although it does not establish general PDE convergence.
